key_insight: A Video Vision Transformer can predict the full viscoelastic droplet impact evolution from only the first 10% to 20% of the simulation, while preserving key flow regimes and geometry.
engineering_relevance: This offers a major reduction in droplet-impact simulation cost, making parametric studies faster for applications like spray cooling, inkjet printing, and pharmaceutical processing.
method: Uses VOF volume-fraction fields as the spatiotemporal input representation.
Trains a ViViT model to extrapolate the remaining droplet dynamics after observing only the initial impact phase.
Targets both Newtonian and viscoelastic effects through parameters such as Re, We, β, and Wi.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximately 80% to 90% computational cost reduction and successful prediction of spreading and bouncing behaviors with good structural similarity.
watch_item: Generalization to real experimental data may be limited unless training includes sufficient measured videos and parameter coverage.
paper_title: Prediction of Viscoelastic Droplet Impact Dynamics Using a Vision Transformer-Based Approach
